newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco's ONA shareholders approve results.
newsitem.headline: Morocco's ONA shareholders approve results.

text.p: Shareholders in Morocco's largest private conglomerate ONA Group, on Wednesday unanimously approved the 1996 consolidated results showing a net profit of $93.4 million.
"The decision was taken during the annual shareholders general assembly in Casablanca, which was also attended by reporters and stockbrokers for the first time,"chairman Fouad Filali .

Despite stagnating turnover due to a sluggish domestic consumption, ONA's consolidated net profit rose 45.8 percent to 878.7 million dirhams ($93.4 million) in 1996 compared with the previous year, Filali said.
"The group continues to concentrate its efforts on the profitability issue...This is why the turnover nearly stagnated last year and might remain unchanged in 1997," he said.
The conglomerate's turnover was down 2.5 percent to 18.11 billion dirhams in 1996 compared with 1995.
According to the indicators of the first six months of 1997, it is expected that "the group will register an improvement of its results this year," Filali told the meeting. He gave no figures.
Analysts at the Casablanca-based Upline Securities stockbroker forecast ONA's net profit 15 percent up to around 1.0 billion dirhams in 1997.
The auditied results showed the ONA continuing to focus on core businesses of international, finance, mining and agro-industry sectors, Gilles Denisty, an ONA manager said.
ONA shares traded 2 dirhams lower at 770, after what Denisty said was an excellent performance in 1996 and early 1997.
The number of traded shares on the bourse jumped from 1.0 million shares in 1995 to 3.0 million shares in 1996, he said.
"ONA's price earning ratio, which was 10.20 at end 1996, remains far below the average 14.19 registered on the Casablanca stock exchange," Filali told shareholders.

ONA's four listed subsidiaries Edible oil firm Lesieur Cristal, sugar refinery Cosumar, agro-industry Centrale Laitiere, and Financiere Diwan showed a rise in net profits at between 344.6 million dirhams and 89.5 million dirhams in 1996 or an improvement of up to 161.5 percent.
The general assembly unanimously approved that ONA pays a dividend of 15 dirhams to its shareholders, up from 14 dirhams in 1995 and 13 dirhams in 1994.
Filali, who is the son of Prime Minister Abdellatif Filali and son-in-law of King Hassan, expects ONA to expand its mining activity described as "the growth engine in 1997".
Established in Casablanca in 1919, ONA has the largest market capitalisation of the 48 listed stocks, and is worth more than 14 billion dirhams ($1.5 billion).
Among the 48 listed stocks on the Casablanca bourse, ONA was last traded at 770 dirhams per share, brokers said.
